{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-21: "now that we've developed the 9 subsystems of reflow2, can we work on coming up with more exhaustive tests for each subsystem? things like edge cases and identify failure modes and other tests."

📌 FIRST, TWO CORRECTIONS OF FACT, both small and both worth having straight before anyone plans work against them. There are TEN subsystems, not nine. And one of them, `cmp:packaging`, carries a `cmp:` id at subsystem level with ZERO components under it — a naming and containment oddity that predates today and is not a defect anyone has been asked about yet.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑🛑 THE FINDING: EXHAUSTIVE TESTS CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DESIGN TODAY, AND THE REASON IS ONE NUMBER
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    Capabilities:                          192
    ... declaring their INPUTS:              3
    ... declaring their OUTPUTS:             3
    ... declaring a SIGNATURE:               0
    Constraints (where a hard limit lives):  1

EDGE CASES ARE DERIVED FROM THE BOUNDARIES OF AN INPUT DOMAIN. FAILURE MODES ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT AN OUTPUT PROMISES. With neither stated for 189 of 192 capabilities, both can only be IMAGINED — which is what 1376 hand-written tests already are, and they are good ones, but imagining more of them is not what "exhaustive" means. `dec:idea-stated-module-function-is-what-makes-failure-mode-testing-derivable` (Anthony, 2026-08-20) said this a day early and named the mechanism: `Capability.inputs`/`outputs` exist in the schema with NO typed tool, NO instruction and NO detector — the three-legged failure again.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND THE PER-SUBSYSTEM PICTURE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY YET
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    subsystem              components   verifications
    sys:coherence-loop         28            68
    sys:agent-surface          25            31
    sys:store                   2            16
    sys:foundation              6            14
    sys:time-history            6            14
    sys:intake                  4             6
    sys:vocabulary              2             6
    cmp:packaging               0             4
    sys:human-channel           2             2
    sys:documentation           1             0

    181 Verifications; 27 of them reach NO subsystem at all.
    127 real test FILES on disk; 47 are pointed at by an Artifact.
    ⇒ 80 TEST FILES THE DESIGN HAS NEVER HEARD OF.

⭐ SO "sys:documentation HAS ZERO VERIFICATIONS" MAY WELL BE FALSE. With 80 of 127 test files unmodelled, a zero in that table is as likely to be a MODELLING gap as a TESTING gap — and acting on it would mean writing tests for something already tested while something genuinely bare stays quiet. **A detector that reports zero because it had nothing to run on reads exactly like one that ran clean**, and this table currently has that defect. Anything built on these counts should re-measure first.

📌 AND THE OTHER AXIS IS STILL UNTOUCHED: 181 of 181 Verifications carry `kind: verification`. ZERO carry `validation`. reflow2 ships the built-right / right-thing split and has never once used it on itself. "More exhaustive" in the built-right direction is already 1376 tests deep; the axis with nothing on it at all is whether each subsystem does the RIGHT thing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) DECLARE THE SHAPE OF THE FUNCTIONS, THEN DERIVE. Populate `inputs`/`outputs` on one subsystem's capabilities, and generate the edge cases from the input boundaries and the failure modes from the output promises. THE ONLY ROUTE ON WHICH "EXHAUSTIVE" MEANS SOMETHING CHECKABLE rather than something claimed. EXPENSIVE, and it needs all three legs built first (a typed tool, an instruction, a detector), because 3-of-192 is what two missing legs look like. Worth doing on ONE subsystem as a trial before committing to ten.

(b) TEST AGAINST THE INTERFACES THAT ALREADY EXIST. 17 Interfaces, 13 carrying a spec — and a spec clause is a failure mode waiting to be written down: violate each clause in turn and assert the refusal. CHEAP AND AVAILABLE NOW. LIMIT, stated plainly: only 4 of the 10 subsystems publish an interface, and the other six present nothing because nothing consumes them. This covers 4 subsystems well and 6 not at all.

(c) START FROM THE THIN ROWS — documentation, human-channel, packaging. Intuitive and probably WRONG as stated, for the reason above: the thin rows are where the MODEL is thinnest, which is not the same as where the TESTING is thinnest. Do not do this without re-measuring.

(d) MAKE THE NUMBERS REAL FIRST. Map the 80 unmodelled test files to Verifications so the per-subsystem table stops being fiction. CHEAPEST OF ALL, mechanical, and it is what every other option's numbers depend on. It adds no tests — which is exactly the objection to it, and the answer is that it tells you where to add them.

(e) THE VALIDATION AXIS. Ask, per subsystem, "does this do the right thing?" rather than "does it do what it says?" — 181 Verifications and not one of them asks it. Different question from the one he asked, and possibly the more valuable one, which is why it is here rather than left out.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Whether declared inputs/outputs would actually yield tests nobody had thought of, or merely restate the ones already written. THAT IS MEASURABLE ON ONE SUBSYSTEM and is the honest gate on (a): declare the shape for `sys:vocabulary` or `sys:store` (2 components each, small enough to finish), derive the cases mechanically, and count how many were NOT already covered by the existing suite. If the answer is near zero, (a) is elaborate bookkeeping and should be dropped.","name":"OPEN — can exhaustive per-subsystem tests be DERIVED, or only imagined? 3 of 192 capabilities state their shape","status":"proposed"}
